review_notes: I read all of BinKernel.lean (lines 1–102). I also checked the uses of binKernelWeight, binKernelConstant, half_le_abs_int_add_half and realBin_kernel_bound across the repo. The file has no @[simp] attributes and no custom simp sets, so it can't create a simp loop or competing rules. Its simp, simp_rw and simpa calls are all `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, and they rewrite in the expected directions. The two noncomputable defs, binKernelWeight and binKernelConstant, are used mainly as opaque constants in bounds. The one place that unfolds binKernelWeight is BinEstimates.lean, line 22, `norm_num [binKernelWeight]`. That is a single use, so I did not recommend a new simp lemma or a positivity lemma for it. Almost all uses of binKernelConstant are as an atom, or through `.toReal` and `binKernelConstant_ne_top`, so a simp lemma there would add no benefit. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out the unfolding in that one `norm_num [binKernelWeight]` call being slightly inefficient. DiagonalBinMassLe.lean (FalconerCompletion/Graphs) contains copies of several declarations from this file. That is a duplication issue, not a simp-interface issue, so I did not report it.
